analysis.title: USA: Philly Fed Manufacturing Declines More Than Expected; Initial Claims Slightly Above Consensus Expectations
key_insights: The Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell 14.6pt to +6.3 in November, the third consecutive monthly decline, well below GS +21.0, median forecast +20.1 and prior +20.9.
The composition was mixed. New orders fell 4.7pt to -0.4, while shipments rose 10.4pt to 25.7 and employment rose 2.5pt to 11.6.
Prices paid rose 15.0pt to 58.2 and prices received rose 6.9pt to 47.0, the highest level for prices received since June 2022.
The delivery times component fell 5.0pt to 3.5, meaning delivery times declined on net. The 6 months-ahead business conditions index rose 0.6pt to 33.6.
Initial jobless claims rose 1k to 203k in the week ended November 14, slightly above the median forecast of 198k and GS 195k. The four-week moving average rose 2k to 198k.
State detail for initial claims: Missouri fell 5k, reversing a spike the prior week, and New Jersey and California each fell 2k.
Continuing claims rose 70k to 1,763k in the week ended November 7, above the median forecast of 1,703k.

Michigan drove much of the rise in continuing claims (+44k) and initial claims (+7k), the largest increases since the pandemic. GS suspects the launch of Michigan's new unemployment insurance platform is the cause, not a genuine softening of the labor market.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Third straight monthly decline, down 14.6pt from +20.9 and well below the +20.1 median forecast. New orders weakened, but shipments and employment improved.
GS expected a small rise from the prior +20.9. The actual print missed by about 15 points.
Consensus expected a roughly flat reading. The actual print was far below it.
Rose 15.0pt, a sharp increase in input cost pressure.
Rose 6.9pt to the highest level since June 2022, a sign of firmer output pricing.
Rose 10.4pt, which offsets part of the weakness in new orders.
Fell 5.0pt, so delivery times declined on net.
Up 1k from the revised prior 202k and slightly above the 198k median forecast. The four-week average rose 2k to 198k.
GS expected a lower figure than the print.
The print came in 5k above consensus.
Up 70k from the revised prior 1,693k and above the 1,703k median forecast. Michigan's new unemployment insurance platform likely inflated the figure.

risk_factors: The Michigan spike in continuing claims may be a platform-launch artifact, so the reading could reverse in later weeks.
Sharp increases in prices paid and prices received point to firmer price pressure in manufacturing.
